title: Fuse a bounded row reduction with its affine producer and consumers

source.title: Triton Layer Normalization tutorial
source.version: commit e721911705a44f634bedc8089b4fe57015e1ffc7, referenced by upstream issue 2243
source.claim_scope: The upstream tutorial demonstrates one-program-per-row LayerNorm reduction and fused affine work. Transfer to RMSNorm, strided views, extra producers/consumers, exact cast boundaries, and current hardware requires operator-specific correctness and timing evidence.

implementation_recipe: Map one independent logical row to one program when the full reduction state fits the implementation limit; mask the power-of-two tail and keep accumulator math in the contract-required precision.
Load each producer input with its actual strides, compute the row summary locally, finalize the reciprocal scale, and apply affine or modulation consumers before storing outputs.
Audit every dtype boundary before fusion. When an intermediate must be bit-exact, explicitly round or materialize at that boundary instead of reassociating producer arithmetic.
Pre-register a multi-stage partial-reduction alternative and shape-specialized dispatch when the row is too wide or the number of rows is too small for useful occupancy.
Measure the fused row, split exact-producer plus row-reduction, and framework-compiled controls before tuning warps or launch parameters.
validation_recipe: Test singleton and non-power-of-two row counts, the maximum supported feature width, and every declared contiguous or strided layout.
Check required intermediate outputs separately from final normalized outputs; use bit equality where the frozen contract requires a cast or rounding boundary.
Measure dominant shapes and optional paths independently, including a small-row launch-latency case and a large-row bandwidth or occupancy case.
Reject a fused variant that improves the weighted mean by regressing a protected case beyond its frozen guard.
expected_bottleneck_shifts: Removed launches and intermediate rereads can shift the kernel to row-reduction latency, register pressure, or memory bandwidth.
At very small row counts, one-program-per-row can expose insufficient parallelism; at very wide rows, local state can exceed practical compiler or register limits.
Explicit strided loads can replace framework materialization but may reduce coalescing and make address generation visible.
failure_modes: Producer fusion changes a required low-precision rounding boundary or floating-point association.
A superficially similar ordered prefix/scan is used even though only a commutative row summary is required.
The complete row is forced into one program after register pressure or row width makes a tiled partial reduction faster.
The implementation assumes contiguous modulation parameters and silently mishandles a legal strided view.
Launch-count reasoning is treated as a numeric performance ceiling without target measurements.
scope_limits: The tutorial's LayerNorm benchmark is not target performance evidence for RMSNorm or a composed model operator.
One-program-per-row is a candidate decomposition, not a universal optimum; multi-stage or persistent decompositions remain open when rows are wide or sparse.
Fusion is legal only across numerical, aliasing, output-materialization, and ABI boundaries allowed by the frozen operator contract.

algorithmic_decomposition.baseline_dependency: A framework expression materializes producer values, launches a row summary reduction, then rereads values and parameters for normalization and affine consumers.
algorithmic_decomposition.partition_axis: Assign independent logical rows to programs; lanes cover the feature axis and reduce a masked FP32 local sum or sum of squares.
local_state: masked row values or recomputable producer values
optional exact-rounded intermediate required by the contract
algorithmic_decomposition.combine_rule: Use the commutative row reduction specified by the operator, such as a sum or sum of squares; do not substitute an ordered prefix decomposition.
algorithmic_decomposition.finalization: Compute the row scale, apply affine/modulation consumers with explicit strides, and store every contract-required output exactly once.
algorithmic_decomposition.work_complexity: O(rows * features) useful arithmetic with no full-size intermediate reread when the contract permits register reuse.
algorithmic_decomposition.span_complexity: One bounded intra-program row reduction plus final elementwise work; use a hierarchical partial reduction when the row cannot fit safely.
algorithmic_decomposition.communication_cost: In the single-row form, no global partial buffer; otherwise one compact summary per tile plus a finalization launch.
invariants: each logical row reduces only its own valid feature elements
masked lanes contribute the reduction identity
all legal input strides and independent output layouts are honored
required low-precision rounding boundaries and protected optional paths are preserved
anti_patterns: apply a prefix-scan card to a commutative row summary
flatten independent rows into a cross-row reduction
erase a mandatory observable intermediate during fusion
tune warps repeatedly without screening split and shape-specialized decompositions

candidate_archetypes.name: one program per logical row
candidate_archetypes.template: Compute the legal producer, local row summary, normalization, and consumers in one row program while explicitly preserving required dtype boundaries.

candidate_archetypes.name: exact producer boundary plus fused row consumer
candidate_archetypes.template: Keep only the producer operations needed for exact intermediate semantics, then fuse the row reduction and remaining consumers.

candidate_archetypes.name: partial summaries plus finalization
candidate_archetypes.template: For wide or under-parallel rows, compute per-tile summaries and combine them before a final normalization/consumer pass.
